library(patchwork) # Arranging Plots
library(ggprism) # Interesting Categorical Axe




Number of people = 1000
Age = Legally, people above 21 onward are allowed to have the bio-computer in their body, since it is the year 2050, the global population is projected to reach 9.7 B, with a significant increase in the elderly age group thus the median will shift from 31 (current) to 36 approx.
Profession = Currently have included 4 profession across various industries such as agriculture, engineering, healthcare and transport according to their need in 2050.
Social connection = Essentially is the number of people a certain person knows.
Access to healthcare = Basically how easy it is for them to get proper healthcare.
Resource availability = Again, takes into consideration how much a person has access to resources ranging from 20-100.


set.seed(123)

n <- 1000

Age <- round(rnorm(n, mean = 36, sd = 15)) 
Age[Age < 21] <- 21  

Gender <- sample(c("Male", "Female"), n, replace=TRUE, prob=c(0.5, 0.5))  # Equal distribution of Male and Female

Professions <- c("Farmer", "Engineer", "Doctor", "Driver")
Profession <- sample(Professions, n, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.2, 0.5, 0.2, 0.1))  

Resources <- runif(n, min = 20, max = 100)

HealthcareAccess <- runif(n, min = 0, max = 1)

BioComputerUser <- sample(c("Yes", "No"), n, replace=TRUE, prob=c(0.3, 0.7))

# Combine everything into a dataframe
society_2050 <- data.frame(
  Age,
  Gender,
  Profession,
  Resources,
  HealthcareAccess,
  BioComputerUser
)

# Check the first few rows
head(society_2050)

  Age Gender Profession Resources HealthcareAccess BioComputerUser
1  28 Female   Engineer  44.35713       0.24862988              No
2  33 Female     Driver  86.62550       0.98946318              No
3  59 Female   Engineer  67.49180       0.71712190              No
4  37   Male     Doctor  84.57573       0.65172829              No
5  38 Female   Engineer  43.52406       0.24055621              No
6  62   Male     Doctor  31.28682       0.08679275             Yes



write.csv(society_2050, "society_2050.csv", row.names=FALSE)


getwd()

[1] "C:/Users/91705/Desktop/R Stuff/2050"






society_2050 <- society_2050 %>%
  mutate(
    Age = as.integer(Age),               # Convert Age to integer
    Profession = as.factor(Profession),    # Convert Profession to factor
    Resources = as.numeric(Resources),    # Convert Resources to numeric
    HealthcareAccess = as.numeric(HealthcareAccess),  # Convert HealthcareAccess to numeric
    BioComputerUser = as.factor(BioComputerUser)  # Convert BioComputerUser to factor
  )

# Check the structure of the modified dataset
glimpse(society_2050)

Rows: 1,000
Columns: 6
$ Age              <int> 28, 33, 59, 37, 38, 62, 43, 21, 26, 29, 54, 41, 42, 3…
$ Gender           <chr> "Female", "Female", "Female", "Male", "Female", "Male…
$ Profession       <fct> Engineer, Driver, Engineer, Doctor, Engineer, Doctor,…
$ Resources        <dbl> 44.35713, 86.62550, 67.49180, 84.57573, 43.52406, 31.…
$ HealthcareAccess <dbl> 0.24862988, 0.98946318, 0.71712190, 0.65172829, 0.240…
$ BioComputerUser  <fct> No, No, No, No, No, Yes, No, Yes, Yes, No, No, No, Ye…











The boxplot showcases how resources are distributed for doctors and engineers, to understand if one profession has consistently higher or lower resources than the other.
The plot shows the range and outliers that are outside the typical range.


# Filter the dataset for Doctors and Engineers
subset_profession <- society_2050[society_2050$Profession %in% c("Doctor", "Engineer"), ]

# Create the box plot
ggplot(subset_profession, aes(x = Profession, y = Resources, fill = Profession)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Resource Distribution: Doctors vs Engineers",
       x = "Profession",
       y = "Resource Availability") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Doctor" = "blue", "Engineer" = "purple")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)









scatter_plot <- plot_ly(
  data = society_2050,
  x = ~Resources,
  y = ~HealthcareAccess,
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "markers",
  color = ~Profession, # Color by Profession (Engineer, Doctor etc.)
  marker = list(opacity = 0.6)
)

# 2D Histogram (Density Plot)
hist2d_plot <- plot_ly(
  data = society_2050,
  x = ~Resources,
  y = ~HealthcareAccess,
  type = "histogram2d"
)

# Combine both plots vertically
fig <- subplot(scatter_plot, hist2d_plot, nrows = 2, shareX = TRUE, shareY = TRUE)

fig






set.seed(123)
society_2050$year <- sample(2020:2050, n, replace = TRUE)

fig <- plot_ly(
  data = society_2050, 
  x = ~Age, 
  y = ~Resources, 
  color = ~HealthcareAccess, 
  size = ~ifelse(BioComputerUser == "Yes", 10, 5),
  text = ~paste("Age:", Age, "<br>Resources:", round(Resources, 2), 
                "<br>Healthcare Access:", round(HealthcareAccess, 2), 
                "<br>BioComputer User:", BioComputerUser),
  frame = ~year,  
  type = 'scatter',
  mode = 'markers',
  marker = list(opacity = 0.6),
  hoverinfo = 'text'
)

fig
